subject: Introduction to Mechanical Engineering
title: Manufacturing Processes and Modern Manufacturing — MCQ Practice
note: Original ACADRIX practice MCQs based on the R-2025 Unit V scope. These are not official university questions or PYQs.

questions.q: Which manufacturing process uses a mould to produce a component from molten material?
questions.explanation: Casting produces a component by pouring molten material into a mould and allowing it to solidify.

questions.q: In casting, the cavity that gives the component its required shape is provided by the what?
questions.explanation: The mould contains the cavity into which molten material is introduced and solidified.

questions.q: Which manufacturing process changes the shape of a workpiece mainly by plastic deformation?
questions.explanation: Forming processes shape material through controlled plastic deformation without primarily removing material.

questions.q: Which process is an example of bulk metal forming?
questions.explanation: Forging is a bulk deformation process in which compressive forces plastically shape the workpiece.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a cutting tool in machining?
options: Remove material to obtain the required shape
questions.answer: Remove material to obtain the required shape
questions.explanation: Machining removes unwanted material using a cutting tool to achieve specified geometry, dimensions and surface finish.

questions.q: Which machining operation is primarily used to produce a cylindrical external surface?
questions.explanation: Turning uses relative rotation between the workpiece and cutting tool and is commonly used for cylindrical surfaces.

questions.q: Which machining process commonly uses a rotating multi-point cutting tool?
questions.explanation: Milling generally uses a rotating cutter having multiple cutting edges to remove material.

questions.q: Which process is primarily used to join two or more components by creating a permanent joint?
questions.explanation: Welding creates a permanent joint by producing coalescence between materials, commonly with heat and sometimes pressure.

questions.q: Which joining process uses a separate filler metal whose melting point is lower than that of the base materials?
questions.explanation: Brazing joins materials using a filler metal that melts above the applicable threshold for brazing while the base materials remain substantially solid.

questions.q: What does CNC stand for?
questions.explanation: CNC refers to Computer Numerical Control, in which machine-tool operations are controlled by programmed numerical instructions.

questions.q: A major advantage of CNC machines is their ability to provide what?
questions.explanation: CNC enables programmed tool motion and repeatable production of complex or precise components.

questions.q: Which manufacturing approach builds a component layer by layer from digital data?
questions.explanation: Additive Manufacturing creates parts by adding material layer by layer according to digital geometry.

questions.q: Which characteristic is strongly associated with Additive Manufacturing?
options: Production of complex geometries directly from digital models
Material removal as the only mechanism
questions.answer: Production of complex geometries directly from digital models
questions.explanation: Additive methods can produce geometrically complex parts that may be difficult to manufacture by conventional processes.

questions.q: What is a key objective of Smart Manufacturing?
options: Use connected data and intelligent technologies to improve manufacturing
questions.answer: Use connected data and intelligent technologies to improve manufacturing
questions.explanation: Smart Manufacturing integrates connected machines, data, sensing, automation and analytics to improve manufacturing performance.

questions.q: Which factor is most important when selecting a manufacturing process?
options: Material, geometry, quantity, accuracy and cost
questions.answer: Material, geometry, quantity, accuracy and cost
questions.explanation: Process selection should consider material, part geometry, production volume, tolerances, surface finish, equipment and economic factors.

questions.q: For a component requiring very high dimensional accuracy and fine surface finish, which consideration becomes especially important?
questions.explanation: The selected process must be capable of meeting required dimensions, tolerances and surface-finish specifications.

questions.q: Which process is generally associated with producing near-net-shape metal parts by pouring molten metal into a cavity?
questions.explanation: Casting can produce complex shapes by filling a mould cavity with molten material and allowing it to solidify.

questions.q: Which manufacturing category primarily removes material from a workpiece?
questions.explanation: Machining is a material-removal manufacturing category in which cutting processes remove unwanted material.

questions.q: Which statement best distinguishes additive manufacturing from conventional machining?
options: Additive manufacturing adds material while machining primarily removes material
Additive manufacturing cannot use digital models
questions.answer: Additive manufacturing adds material while machining primarily removes material
questions.explanation: The fundamental distinction is the direction of material usage: additive processes build material, whereas machining removes material.

questions.q: In a manufacturing route, why are multiple processes sometimes combined?
options: Different processes may be needed for shape, accuracy, finish and joining requirements
Every component must use every process
questions.answer: Different processes may be needed for shape, accuracy, finish and joining requirements
questions.explanation: A complete manufacturing route may combine processes because one process may establish shape while another achieves accuracy, finish or assembly requirements.

questions.q: Which manufacturing approach can use sensors, connectivity and data analytics for real-time process monitoring?
questions.explanation: Smart Manufacturing uses connected equipment, sensors and data systems to monitor and optimize manufacturing operations.

questions.q: Which CNC-related feature allows the same programmed sequence to be reproduced for multiple components?
questions.explanation: A programmed CNC sequence can be executed repeatedly, supporting consistent production when process conditions are controlled.

questions.q: Which joining method is commonly associated with using a filler metal and capillary action without melting the base metals?
questions.explanation: Brazing uses a molten filler metal that flows into the joint, commonly by capillary action, while the base materials are not melted.

questions.q: Which factor can make Additive Manufacturing attractive for low-volume customized components?
options: Reduced dependence on dedicated tooling for many geometries
Requirement for a unique mould for every layer
questions.answer: Reduced dependence on dedicated tooling for many geometries
questions.explanation: Digital manufacturing can reduce the need for dedicated tooling when producing customized or low-volume geometrically complex parts.

questions.q: Which statement represents good manufacturing-process selection?
options: Choose the process that meets technical requirements while remaining economically suitable
Always choose the most expensive process
questions.answer: Choose the process that meets technical requirements while remaining economically suitable
questions.explanation: Good process selection balances technical requirements such as material, geometry, accuracy and finish with production volume, equipment and cost.
